name: Lenskart · Omnichannel payments
blurb: How a listed Indian eyewear retailer turns a counter swipe, an app payment or a bag of cash into booked revenue and treasury liquidity.
chapters: 1 · The order and the tender
The customer chooses frames and lenses; the billing app creates an invoice and records how it is paid (card, UPI, cash, or a mix).
Every later match depends on this record carrying an order ID and tender split.
Wrong tender split, duplicate invoice.
2 · Authorisation
Card taps go from the terminal to the acquirer, card network and issuer; UPI goes through NPCI; online payments go through a gateway such as Razorpay or PhonePe.
Authorisation proves the customer can pay, but no money has reached Lenskart yet.
Declines, timeouts, pending UPI.
3 · Settlement
Aggregators hold funds in escrow, deduct MDR plus GST, and pay out the net, typically T+1. Cash waits in the store safe, then goes by CIT van to a bank branch.
This is where gross sales shrink to net cash, and where float (money in transit) sits.
Held settlements, short cash counts.
4 · Landing in the bank
Credits arrive in Lenskart bank accounts, possibly tagged by VAN per store. The bank sends a daily statement file with reference text.
Clean references make automatic matching possible.
Credits with no reference, wrong store.
5 · Reconciliation
Three records are compared: the invoice register, the aggregator/CIT report, and the bank statement. Matches are booked; mismatches go to suspense.
Proves every rupee of revenue is real cash and exposes leakage early.
Ageing suspense, unmatched UPI.
6 · Treasury and outflows
Balances are swept to a master account, then pay franchise partners, factories, vendors, payroll and taxes; surplus is invested per policy.
Turns collections into usable liquidity; for 306 franchise stores, the netting formula matters.
Wrong netting, idle cash, FX on overseas cash.

parties.role: Each country uses its own acquirers, QR schemes and bank accounts; funds sit in local entity accounts first.
Network routes authorisation to the issuing bank; clearing and settlement go to the acquirer. Interchange + scheme + acquirer fee make up MDR.
NPCI switch moves UPI P2M between remitter bank and beneficiary PSP bank. MDR on UPI P2M has been zero under current policy — verify before modelling fees.
RBI payment-aggregator rules require merchant funds to sit in an escrow with a scheduled bank until settled; fees and GST netted here.
CIT deposits notes against the store or entity account reference.
Illustrative: your brief uses HDFC and a VAN per store. Real bank and structure are not public. Virtual accounts let one account serve many stores.
Matches invoice register ↔ aggregator/CIT report ↔ bank credit; books sales, fees, tax; parks breaks in suspense. ERP vendor not public.
Franchise settlements (306 FOFO stores), supplier and factory payments, payroll for ~17.6k staff.
Receives sweeps, funds outflows, parks surplus per policy; cross-border upstream from subsidiaries.
Output GST on sales less ITC, TDS on payments, quarterly advance tax; paid via bank/govt portals.
